notes: A gamepad and a keyboard are peers here, not a primary and a fallback, and which one is
live is decided by which the player last touched rather than by a settings screen.
The two blocks are separate because a stick and a key are different instruments. A stick
reports a continuous position and needs a dead zone and a response curve; a key reports on
or off and needs a ramp to become steering at all. Sharing one set of numbers makes one of
the two feel wrong, and which one depends on whose machine it was tuned on.
InputBindings.defaults() holds these same values, and a test asserts the two agree — the
code copy exists so a missing file leaves a playable game rather than a car that ignores

_mapping.aim: right stick (as a rate, not a position)

_why: steerExponent above 1 buys precision where it is spent: full lock is a rare input and
the first ten degrees are most of the driving.
aimRate exists because a stick reports a position and aiming needs a velocity — treating
the position as an absolute angle snaps the reticle back to centre when you let go.

analogueTriggerAxis* default to -1, meaning the digital L2/R2 buttons every backend supports. gdx-controllers 2.x's portable mapping has no trigger axes and the real indices vary by pad and platform, so a machine with analogue triggers sets them here rather than the code guessing.
Return is more than twice the ramp on purpose. Held input builds progressively and
letting go recentres immediately, which is what makes a keyboard driveable at speed
rather than a series of stabs the car never settles between.
